patch.value: Health result contract parity: every checks[] row exposes a boolean ok beside its tri-state status

GitHub #980 shows that the public health result uses ok:boolean on the envelope but status:ok|warn|fail with no ok property on each checks[] row. Natural agent code reuses row.ok and can report every healthy check as failed or construct a gate that never fires. This is a public SDK result-schema consistency and compatibility issue, not a change to the established meaning of the aggregate health verdict. Duplicate check searched all statuses for health JSON, checks row ok/status, envelope boolean, and the linked GH-785/GH-815 verdict issues; no item owns row-level boolean parity.

The public HealthCheck result type exposes ok:boolean on every checks[] row while preserving status:ok|warn|fail; ok has one documented derivation from status and aggregate advisory/blocking policy remains unchanged; SDK, CLI JSON, MCP, compact/full projections, contracts, fixtures, and docs agree; compatibility tests prove existing status consumers are unchanged and naive row.ok predicates identify failures correctly; packaged npm/npx/bun/bunx acceptance, exact 100/100/100/100 coverage, docstrings, and static gates pass
Make the public SDK health result self-consistent and safe for naive automation at every nesting level
Agents can inspect failing health checks without silently inverting or disabling their gate predicate
SDK, CLI JSON, MCP, and extension consumers share one backward-compatible truth signal per check
The mismatch reproduces in current published packages and lies on the failure-investigation path used by release automation
Run pm health --json and compare top-level .ok with .checks[0].ok and .checks[0].status; .checks[0].ok is absent while status is ok
Each checks[] entry carries a boolean ok compatible with the envelope spelling, alongside its existing tri-state status
The envelope has ok:boolean while each check has only status:string, allowing missing-key falsiness to invert or disable obvious agent gates
